title: Rent assistance -- who this is for and why
description: The authored Needs Document paired with the lifecycle-demo bundle, adapted from needs-spec Appendix A onto this spike's exemplar. One record per line of the brief, plus one candidate an agent filed from a support queue and nobody has ruled on yet. Statements are written to the JOURNEYS.md plain-language bar: a policy officer must be able to read each one on first contact.

journeys.title: The Applicant
journeys.description: The person applying for help with rent. Usually on a phone, usually under a deadline, often after a bad week.

journeys.title: The Caseworker
journeys.description: The person at the agency who decides. Works a queue, answers the phone, and carries the consequences of a lost file.

statement.who: anyone submitting this application under a deadline
statement.want: a receipt I can save and show someone later
statement.why: if the agency loses my submission, I lose help I was entitled to and I cannot prove I asked in time
statement.done: after I submit, I hold a receipt that proves what I filed and when -- and it still proves it if the agency's system is gone

grounding.description: The retention obligation any receipt has to satisfy. Rulespec owns everything behind this identifier; this document only cites it.

excerpt.exact: I screenshot every confirmation page because they lost my renewal once.
excerpt.prefix: Do you keep anything after you apply?

needs.title: Signing without a trip to the office

statement.who: anyone who has to swear that what they wrote is true
statement.want: to sign right here, without printing anything or going anywhere
statement.why: a trip across town to sign a piece of paper is how people with no car and no spare hours fall out of the process
statement.done: I sign on the device I am already holding, and I am told in plain words what I just signed

grounding.description: What makes an electronic signature count here at all. Cited, never restated.

statement.who: the person at the agency who has to decide this case
statement.want: everything the applicant sent, in one place, in the order I need it
statement.why: when I have to chase missing pages, the family waits weeks longer for a decision I could have made on day one
statement.done: I open a case and either decide it or say exactly what is missing, without sending an email

excerpt.exact: Half of what I do is asking people for something they already sent.

statement.who: anyone applying from a place with unreliable internet
statement.want: the application to keep working when my connection drops
statement.why: the people who need this help most often have the worst connections, so a dropped signal turns into a lost application
statement.done: a dropped connection never costs me my answers

needs.title: Being told why the answer was no

statement.who: anyone whose application was turned down
statement.want: to be told in plain words why, and what I can do about it
statement.why: a refusal nobody explains is a refusal nobody can appeal, and the people it hits hardest are the ones least able to ask twice
statement.done: when the answer is no, I can read the reason and I know what my next step is

excerpt.exact: Callers rarely dispute the decision. They call because the letter does not say which rule they failed.

statement.who: anyone filling this in on a phone
statement.want: to start on my phone and finish later on a computer
statement.why: losing twenty minutes of answers means many people never come back at all
statement.done: when I come back on any device, my answers are where I left them

excerpt.exact: Drop-off concentrates at the document-upload step on mobile sessions.
